At Chaxa, bright salt flats meet shallow water. Flamingos can be observed here, as the lagoons of the salt flat provide their natural habitat.

Chaxa is part of Los Flamencos National Reserve. It is visited on routes across the Atacama Salt Flat, often after exploring the high-altitude lagoons of Miscanti and Miñiques.

The final ascent to Laguna de los Tres is worth making for the moment when turquoise water appears beyond the rocky rim. The granite walls of Fitz Roy and neighboring sharp peaks rise above the lake, with white glaciers below them. The trees are left behind, and at the shore the cold wind, stone and proximity of the high mountains become especially vivid.

This is one of the main hiking routes around El Chaltén in Los Glaciares National Park. Along the way, forested sections give way to open mountain views, and the final stretch demands considerable effort. Set aside a full day for this hike. The group's pace and trail conditions matter more than reaching a particular point by a fixed hour: snow, wind and cloud cover affect both the route and visibility.

On Ada Tours' "Argentina, Chile and Beautiful Patagonia" tour, the hike begins at Hostería El Pilar after a transfer from El Chaltén. The approach goes through the forest along the Blanco River. This is one particular route option, not a mandatory itinerary for every visitor. For a trip here, choose comfortable trekking boots and clothing suitable for changeable weather. At the lake, it is tempting to linger for as long as your energy and the mountain conditions allow.

The lake owes its name, "Emerald Lagoon," to the unusual greenish-turquoise shade of its water. The color is particularly vivid in sunny weather, contrasting sharply with the dark forests and snow-covered peaks of the surrounding mountains.

The trail to the lagoon passes through the scenic forests of Tierra del Fuego. As you climb, the landscape gradually changes: dense trees give way to more open areas, rocky paths and peat bogs. The route takes on a very different character depending on the season: green and colorful in summer, but snow-covered in winter, when it becomes a true winter adventure.

The Ojos del Albino and Sierra Escalonada mountains rise around the lagoon, with panoramic views of the southern Andes in the distance. Only the wind and sounds of nature disturb the quiet, making a walk to Laguna Esmeralda especially appealing to those seeking the wild, untouched side of Patagonia.

The hike to the lagoon is considered one of the popular trekking routes near Ushuaia. In just a few hours, it offers a range of Tierra del Fuego landscapes, from forests and peat bogs to a high-altitude lake surrounded by mountains.

Laguna Esmeralda is a little jewel at the end of the world, where emerald water, southern forests and rugged mountains form one of Tierra del Fuego's most memorable landscapes.
